findings.reason: the worker grading the gate maps each control to the case it must turn red, so a mis-numbered control sends it to test a case its mutation leaves green, and the gate then reads as unproven or as passing for the wrong reason; the fix is to re-number the three references (third→fourth, fifth→sixth, sixth→seventh) and state the followup sites' write order explicitly.
findings.text: the five negative controls are numbered against a case list that does not match the seven cases just enumerated: "leave the followup op sites unchecked … the third case's first two writes" names case 3 (edit_plan append and section-move reason), whose writes are not followup sites and which has two writes, not three; "matching a bare `§N` reports the fifth case" names case 5 (`sections.<id>.body` must be refused), which a broader pattern cannot falsify because it already expects a refusal — the case that measures over-matching is case 6 (`landed in §4` must not be reported); and "dropping the `<code>` exemption reports the sixth case" names case 6 where case 7 (`<code>` must not be reported) is the one it falsifies. Read literally, two of the five controls exercise the wrong case and one exercises a case that cannot fail under its mutation.
